spec: Given a string s, count its alphabetic characters as vowels (a, e, i, o, u, case-insensitive) or consonants (any other letter). Non-letter characters (digits, spaces, punctuation) are ignored. Return a dict with keys 'vowels' and 'consonants' mapping to their respective counts. An empty string, or one with no letters, returns {'vowels': 0, 'consonants': 0}.

Sort the keys of d alphabetically, then cyclically shift the values n positions to the right along that key order (so the value that was n positions before a key's slot moves into it; negative n shifts left). Return a new dict with the same keys mapping to the rotated values. An empty dict returns an empty dict.

Given a dict of numbers, sort its keys and compute the running (prefix) sum of values in that sorted key order. Return a dict mapping each key to the cumulative sum of all values for keys less than or equal to it (in sorted order). An empty dict returns an empty dict.

Split the entries of d into two dicts based on their numeric value: one containing entries with a strictly positive value, and one containing entries with a value less than or equal to zero. Return a tuple of (positive_dict, nonpositive_dict). An empty dict returns two empty dicts.

Given two dicts f and g representing mappings, build the composed mapping x -> g[f[x]] for every key x of f whose value f[x] is itself a key of g. Keys of f whose value is not found in g are omitted from the result. An empty f, or no matching keys, returns an empty dict.

Given two equal-length lists keys and values, build a dict by pairing them positionally. If a key appears more than once, keep the value from its first occurrence and ignore later ones. Empty lists return an empty dict.

Given two equal-length lists keys and values, build a dict by pairing them positionally. If a key appears more than once, keep the value from its last occurrence, overwriting earlier ones. Empty lists return an empty dict.

Given a list of strings each formatted as 'key<sep>value' (splitting only on the first occurrence of sep so the value may itself contain sep), parse them into a dict. If the same key appears more than once, keep the value from its first occurrence. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given a list of strings each formatted as 'key<sep>value' (splitting only on the first occurrence of sep so the value may itself contain sep), parse them into a dict. If the same key appears more than once, keep the value from its last occurrence. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given a non-empty list of dicts (rows) that all share the same set of keys, transpose it into a dict of lists (a column-oriented table): each key maps to a list of its values across the rows, in the original row order. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given a list of (key, value) tuples, build a dict mapping each key to a list of all the values associated with it, in the order they were encountered, keeping duplicate values (unlike a set-based grouping). An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given a list of (key, value) tuples with numeric values, sum only the strictly positive values for each key, ignoring entries whose value is zero or negative. Return a dict mapping each key that had at least one positive value to that sum; keys with no positive values are omitted entirely. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given a list of (key, value) tuples with numeric values, compute the average value for each distinct key, rounded to 2 decimal places. Return a dict mapping each key to its average. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given a list of dicts with numeric values, compute for each key that appears in at least one dict the minimum and maximum value seen for it across all dicts that contain it. Return a dict mapping each such key to a tuple (min, max). An empty list returns an empty dict.
Given a dict mapping keys to non-empty lists of numbers, compute the range (max minus min) of each list. Return a dict mapping each key to that range. An empty dict returns an empty dict.

Given a list of dicts with numeric values, compute for every key that appears in at least one dict the average of its value across ALL the dicts in the list, treating a dict that is missing the key as contributing 0 (so the divisor is always the total number of dicts, not just those containing the key). Round each average to 2 decimal places. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given a list of dicts, return a sorted list of the keys that appear in exactly two of the dicts in the list (counting a key once per dict it appears in). An empty list, or one with no such keys, returns an empty list.

Given a base dict and an overrides dict, return a new dict equal to base but with the value of every key that exists in BOTH base and overrides replaced by the overrides value. Keys present only in overrides (not already in base) are ignored and not added. The original base dict is not mutated.

Given a list of dicts, build a dict mapping each key seen in any of them to a list of all the values recorded for that key, in the order the dicts appear (a dict missing a key simply contributes nothing for it). An empty list returns an empty dict.
Given a list seq, build a dict mapping each distinct element to the index of its first occurrence in the list. An empty list returns an empty dict.
Given a list seq, build a dict mapping each distinct element to the index of its last occurrence in the list. An empty list returns an empty dict.

Given a list seq of numbers and bounds low and high, consider only the elements whose value falls within the inclusive range [low, high]. Return a dict mapping each such qualifying distinct value to a sorted list of the indices at which it occurs in seq. Elements outside the range are ignored entirely. An empty list, or no elements in range, returns an empty dict.

Given a list seq of comparable values, find the distinct element that occurs the fewest times. If several elements are tied for the lowest count, return the smallest such element. An empty list returns None.

Given a dict d and a mapping dict from old key names to new key names, return a new dict where every key found in mapping is replaced by its corresponding new name, and every key not in mapping is kept unchanged. If two keys end up mapping to the same new name, the later one (in d's iteration order) wins. An empty d returns an empty dict.

Given a list of dicts records and a mapping dict from old key names to new key names, apply the renaming to every dict in the list (each key found in mapping is replaced, others kept unchanged), returning a new list of renamed dicts in the same order. An empty list returns an empty list.

Given a list of 2-element tuples, group the second elements by the first, preserving the order in which they appeared (including duplicates). Return a dict mapping each distinct first element to a list of its corresponding second elements. An empty list returns an empty dict.
Given a list of strings, count how many strings have each distinct length. Return a dict mapping each length to the number of strings of that length. An empty list returns an empty dict.
Given a list of (name, score) tuples, build a dict mapping each distinct name to the highest score recorded for it in the list. An empty list returns an empty dict.
Given a dict with string keys, find the maximum key length, then return a sorted list of all keys that have that length (there may be one or several). An empty dict returns an empty list.
Given a non-empty dict whose values are lists, find the key whose list is the longest. If several keys tie for the longest list, return the alphabetically smallest such key.

Given a sparse dict mapping non-negative integer indices to values, and a target length, build a dense list of that length filled with 0 by default, placing each sparse value at its index (indices outside [0, length) are ignored). A length of 0 returns an empty list.
Given a list of numbers, build a dict mapping each index whose value is non-zero to that value, omitting zero entries entirely. An empty list, or one full of zeros, returns an empty dict.

Given a dict mapping keys to lists of tags, where each tag is assumed to belong to at most one key across the whole dict, build the reverse mapping: each tag maps to the single key that listed it. Return this tag-> key dict. An empty dict, or one where no key has any tags, returns an empty dict.
Pad a string on the left with spaces so its total length equals width. If the string is already at least as long as width, return it unchanged. Width is a non-negative integer.
Pad a string on the right with spaces so its total length equals width. If the string is already at least as long as width, return it unchanged. Width is a non-negative integer.

Format an integer as a string zero-padded to a total width, keeping a leading minus sign for negative numbers outside the padded digits. If the number already needs at least width characters, return it without truncation.
Given a list of strings and a column width, right-align each string within that width and join them with a single space between columns.
Given a list of text lines and a width, center each line within that width (extra padding, if any, goes on the right) and return the list of centered lines in the same order.

Convert a non-negative integer to its uppercase hexadecimal representation (no prefix) as a string, zero-padded on the left to the given width. If the hex representation is already at least width characters, return it without truncation.
Given a list of string cells and a matching list of column widths, left-justify each cell within its corresponding width and join the results with a single space.
